function.description: Executes a system-level command using os.system() on Windows operating systems. It can execute single or multiple commands chained with '&&'. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

command.description: The system command to be executed. To execute multiple commands, separate them with '&&'. For example, 'dir && echo done'.

unit.description: Specifies the unit of measure for the command if applicable. This is not utilized by os.system() directly but can be used for logging or analysis purposes.

message.content:
I don’t have a way to see your connection from here, but you can quickly find out your current download/upload speeds yourself.  
Below are a few options you can try, depending on what’s available on your machine.

---

## 1️⃣ Quick test with **speedtest‑cli** (Python)

If you already have `speedtest-cli` installed, just run:

```bash
speedtest-cli --simple
```

That will print something like:

```
Ping: 12.34 ms
Download: 123.45 Mbit/s
Upload: 67.89 Mbit/s
```

### Installing `speedtest-cli`

If you don’t have it yet, you can install it with `pip`:

```bash
pip install speedtest-cli
```

or, if you’re on a Debian/Ubuntu system:

```bash
sudo apt-get update
sudo apt-get install speedtest-cli
```

---

## 2️⃣ One‑liner without installing anything (if you have Python)

```bash
python -m pip install --quiet speedtest-cli && python -c "import speedtest; s=speedtest.Speedtest(); s.get_best_server(); print(f'Ping: {s.results.ping:.2f} ms\nDownload: {s.results.download/1e6:.2f} Mbit/s\nUpload: {s.results.upload/1e6:.2f} Mbit/s')"
```

This installs `speedtest-cli` temporarily and runs a quick test.

---

## 3️⃣ Using a browser‑based test

If you prefer a GUI, just open one of these sites in your browser:

- https://www.speedtest.net/
- https://fast.com/
- https://www.fast.com/ (Netflix’s test)

Click “Go” or “Start Test” and wait for the results.

---

## 4️⃣ Windows PowerShell (no extra tools)

If you’re on Windows and want a quick PowerShell snippet, you can use the built‑in `Test-NetConnection` cmdlet to ping a server:

```powershell
Test-NetConnection -ComputerName google.com -InformationLevel Detailed
```

It won’t give you bandwidth, but it will show latency and packet loss.

---

### What to do next

1. Pick one of the methods above that fits your setup.  
2. Run the command or open the website.  
3. Note the download/upload speeds and ping.  

If you run into any errors or need help interpreting the results, just let me know!
